newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Finance Ministry to cut 1997 spending - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thai Finance Ministry to cut 1997 spending - paper.

text.p: The Thai Finance Ministry has ordered a cut of between 20 and 25 billion baht (US$80-100 million) in government spending for fiscal 1997, which began on October 1, the Nation reported on Thursday.
The cut is aimed at balancing an expected shortfall in revenue and will cover regular expenses, arms spending and investment in new projects, the newspaper said.

"Tax revenue in the 1997 fiscal year is forecast to be about 20 to 25 billion baht below anticipated expenditures," Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda was quoted as saying by the newspaper. "The government must control spending and maintain a balanced budget policy for the next government," he said.
Thailand is holding a general election on November 17.
The sitting government has budgeted expenditures at 984 billion baht for fiscal 1997.
